evidence.section_title: Treating depressive symptoms  in schoolchildren A pilot study
evidence.quote: [/page/0/Text/7] revealed a significant improvement on the Children Depression Inventory

[/page/1/Text/10] Next,a clinical interview,based on the DSM-III-R criteria [4], was administered by an independent psychologist. The objective of the study was to focus on children with a sub-threshold depressive profile.A cut-off score was chosen according to Kovacs [37]. Therefore, the study included children showing depressive symptoms on a screening questionnaire and/or a Tscore on a parent measure above a cut-off, and at least one criterion of a Major Depressive Disorder, but without other apparent axis-I problems.

[/1/Text/15] The CDI is used for children aged 7 to 17 and includes 27 items measuring cognitive, affective and behavioural symptoms of depression in children.; [/2/Text/3] The SPPC is a 36-item measure for children aged 8 to 12, surveying children's perceived competence across five specific domains – academic competence, social acceptance, athletic competence, physical appearance, behavioural conduct – as well as global self-worth.
[/page/2/Text/6] A T-score ≥ 63 on the Internalising subscale and the subscale Anxious/Depressed was used as the cut-off score.

[/page/3/Text/8] There were no baseline differences between the children from the treatment group and those from the WL control group for age, scores on the CDI, CBCL total score, CBCL sub-scale Anxious/Depressed, CBCL sub-scale Internalising Problems, STAIC and SPPC Global Self-worth scale.

[/page/3/Text/12] The analyses of the CBCL sub-scale Internalisation Problems revealed no significant group, time, or interaction (group time) effects. [/page/3/Text/13] Significant time effects were found on the SPPC subscale Global Self-worth and on the CDI scores. [/page/3/Text/14] No significant effects were found on the STAIC and CBCL sub-scales Anxious/Depressed between the pretest and the post-test.

CDI (Children's Depression Inventory) is an outcome measure (99); CBCL sub-scale Internalising Problems and Anxious/Depressed are outcome measures (99); SPPC sub-scale Global Selfworth relates to self-esteem, a negative cognition (1); STAIC (State-Trait Anxiety Inventory for Children) does not fit a specific mediator category or depression outcome.
